result.notes:
SKELETON STATE FOUND ON DISK (I authored tests against it; changed no interface/signature): IEnvironment.GetBaseDirectory() already exists on the contract; EnvironmentAdapter.GetBaseDirectory() is the throwing stub (throw new NotSupportedException() at EnvironmentAdapter.cs:49 — the repo uses NotSupportedException, not NotImplementedException, because MA0025 sanctions it as the unimplemented-stub throw); FakeEnvironment already has the _baseDirectory field, the baseDirectory Create parameter, and a NAIVE body (GetBaseDirectory() => _baseDirectory) with NO Decision-5 separator termination yet. AG0035 was already extended to list "baseDirectory" (Rule 2, from RULE-PHASE). So my 4 tests all compile and are RED now: the two real-value tests via the throwing stub; the two fake tests via wrong/expanded behavior (no separator append).

WHAT I AUTHORED: two files, both directly under tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/ (NOT under Presence/), so they are un-gated and run on the macOS, Linux, and Windows CI legs (CI runs the whole solution on each leg). Covers acceptance #6 and #8 — the only two "author a test" criteria. #1/#2/#4/#5/#7 are build/aggregate/analyzer+grep/diff/coverage gate checks, not test-authorable. #3 is the pre-existing Linux-gated PolkitPolicyIntegrityTests whose rewrite the contract explicitly assigns to IMPLEMENT (step 5); its RED forcing functions (Rule-1 analyzer + throwing adapter) are already in place, and it is not exercisable on a macOS host.

AG0035 COMPLIANCE: no test passes a compile-time literal to any FakeEnvironment.Create root parameter. Seeds are runtime reads — real().Environment.GetHomeDirectory() (with a TrimEnd(separator) to guarantee no trailing separator for the explicit-seed RED). The separator compared against is the owned IPlatformFileSystem.DirectorySeparator (never a hardcoded '/'), so every assertion is OS-correct on all three legs.

"ASSERT THE FAKE" IS CORRECT HERE, NOT A MOCK-ASSERTION VIOLATION: Decision 5 / check 8 make FakeEnvironment.GetBaseDirectory()'s separator-termination a REQUIRED production behavior and name "the fake seeded explicitly" and "the fake on its DEFAULT path" as mandatory inputs. FakeEnvironment is therefore the system-under-test for those facts (its own real behavior), not a collaborator mock configured-then-asserted. The real EnvironmentAdapter is driven by the other two facts.

TWO-SIDEDNESS NOTE (rail 4 vs rail 2): Decision 5's rule is "test the value for a trailing separator and append when absent." The append-when-absent side is authored RED (both fake facts). The complementary "already-terminated -> leave unchanged / no double-append" side is COINCIDENTALLY already satisfied by the naive skeleton (=> _baseDirectory), so a standalone test of it would be GREEN-now — a rail-2 (RED-before-green) violation. Criterion #8's literal words require only "ends in a directory separator" for the three named inputs, which I cover RED; I derived strictly from the criterion and deliberately did not add a green idempotence test. The explicit-seed fact uses .Be(seed + separator) (exactly one appended), which also pins that no MORE than one separator is added.

LOCAL PROOF LIMITS: run on macOS/arm64 host with dotnet 10.0.400. The Linux-gated PolkitPolicyIntegrityTests (#3) cannot compile/run here; its proving ground is the CI Linux leg (consistent with the run-record note that OS-gated tests are only measurable on their own legs). No commit, no push. Only tests/ changes are the two new untracked files; the FakeEnvironment.cs "modified" status in git predates this stage (ARCHITECTURE) and I did not touch it.

findings.summary: BaseDirectorySeparatorTests.cs computes the identical setup expression `real.Platform.FileSystem.DirectorySeparator` fresh in all three test methods instead of hoisting it once, even though the class already hoists the other shared value (`real`) into a field and the sibling test class in the same project does exactly this hoisting for a per-test-shared value.
findings.evidence: tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/BaseDirectorySeparatorTests.cs:28, :40, :56 — `char separator = real.Platform.FileSystem.DirectorySeparator;` repeated verbatim (same RHS, same variable name) in RealBaseDirectory_EndsWithADirectorySeparator, FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededWithoutATrailingSeparator_AppendsExactlyOne, and FakeBaseDirectory_OnTheDefaultHomeFallbackPath_EndsWithADirectorySeparator. Contrast tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/PlatformFileSystemSpecTests.cs:23-34, the sibling spec class in the same test project, which hoists an equally reused value (`fileSystem = services.Platform.FileSystem;`) into a field in its constructor precisely to avoid recomputing it per-test — the established local convention this file departs from.
findings.fix: Add `private readonly char separator = SystemServicesBuilder.Real().Build().Platform.FileSystem.DirectorySeparator;` (or derive it from the existing `real` field: `private readonly char separator;` set in a constructor as `real.Platform.FileSystem.DirectorySeparator`) as a class field alongside the existing `private readonly ISystemServices real = ...` field, and delete the three duplicate local `char separator = ...` lines, referencing the field directly in all three test bodies.

refutationAttempts: Checked whether both files independently calling `SystemServicesBuilder.Real().Build()` (BaseDirectoryAccessorTests.cs:22 and BaseDirectorySeparatorTests.cs:23) is a cross-file DRY violation: grepped `SystemServicesBuilder.Real()` across tests/ and found 30+ call sites across the suite (ProcessArchitectureTests.cs, BoundariesEnvironmentAdapterTests.cs, PlatformFileSystemSpecTests.cs, etc.), each building it locally with no shared fixture/base class anywhere in the project (`IClassFixture` has zero real hits, only stale xunit binaries). This is the single approved owner-call pattern per SystemServicesBuilder's own doc comment ('the single approved way a test builds the ISystemServices container') — calling the one owner repeatedly is reuse, not duplication. Rejected as a finding.

Checked whether the repeated one-line FluentAssertions shape (`X.GetBaseDirectory().Should().EndWith(separator.ToString(), "...")` in test 1 and test 3 of BaseDirectorySeparatorTests.cs) is a duplicated assertion block: subjects differ (real.Environment vs fakeDefault), reason strings differ, and this single-line assert-with-message idiom recurs identically in this shape throughout the entire test suite (every FluentAssertions call in the repo). Extracting a one-line assertion into a helper would fight the codebase's own idiom rather than collapse real duplication. Rejected.

Grepped for an existing shared 'directory separator' test helper the new tests should have reused instead of inlining the field access: `grep -rn DirectorySeparator tests/` turned up exactly one prior single-occurrence use (BoundariesSystemServicesWiringTests.cs:39, one test, no repetition) and the owned interface member itself (IPlatformFileSystem.DirectorySeparator) — no shared helper exists to have reused, so 'new' local field-hoisting is the correct fix, not calling into a missed existing owner.

The two new test files only prove the new IEnvironment accessor's plumbing in isolation; the actual test this whole contract exists to fix is untouched and still broken.
findings.evidence: tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/Presence/Linux/PolkitPolicyIntegrityTests.cs:29 (path still built from RepoRoot()) and :55 (`private static string RepoRoot([CallerFilePath] string here = "")` — unchanged, contract step 5 not applied). tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests.csproj — full file read, no `<None Include="...agentguard-presence.policy" CopyToOutputDirectory=...>` item (contract step 4 not applied), so the shipped policy would not even be present in the test output on any leg. `grep -rn "CallerFilePath\|Assembly.Location" tests/ src/` → exactly one hit, PolkitPolicyIntegrityTests.cs:55, meaning acceptance criterion 4 fails as stated today. Consequence for criterion 1: analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/NoCallerFilePathAnalyzer.cs declares AG0039 as `defaultSeverity: DiagnosticSeverity.Warning, isEnabledByDefault: true`, and Directory.Build.props:36 sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` — so on the Linux CI leg (the only leg where this file compiles), AG0039 will fire as a build ERROR against line 55, meaning `dotnet build` will NOT be 0 warnings/0 errors there. Since the IMPLEMENT stage has test-writing authority revoked (per the pipeline's separation of powers), no later stage can legally make this edit — it is TDD's responsibility and it was skipped.
findings.fix: Rewrite PolkitPolicyIntegrityTests.cs per contract step 5: replace the line-29 path build with `Path.Combine(services.Environment.GetBaseDirectory(), "agentguard-presence.policy")` (services = the existing `SystemServicesBuilder.Real().Build()` at line 28), delete the `RepoRoot()` helper and the now-unused `System.Runtime.CompilerServices` using, and update the class doc. Add the `CopyToOutputDirectory` item for `eng/polkit/agentguard-presence.policy` to `AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests.csproj` per contract step 4. Both are test-file/test-project changes and must land in the TDD deliverable.

findings.summary: Decision 5's separator logic has two branches — append the separator when absent, leave the value alone when already present — but only the 'absent' branch is pinned with an exact-equality assertion; nothing proves the fake does not double the separator when the seed is already terminated.
findings.evidence: tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/BaseDirectorySeparatorTests.cs:37-51 (`FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededWithoutATrailingSeparator_AppendsExactlyOne` — seed has its trailing separator stripped before use) and :53-65 (`FakeBaseDirectory_OnTheDefaultHomeFallbackPath_EndsWithADirectorySeparator` — the home fallback also normally lacks a trailing separator, and is checked only with `EndWith`, not exact equality). No fact anywhere seeds `FakeEnvironment.Create` with a `baseDirectory` that already ends in the separator and asserts the returned value is unchanged rather than doubled.
findings.fix: Add a fourth fact, e.g. `FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededWithATrailingSeparator_DoesNotAppendASecondOne`, seeding `FakeEnvironment.Create(seed, baseDirectory: seed + separator)` and asserting `fake.GetBaseDirectory()` equals exactly `seed + separator` (not doubled).
